subject: WRITE statement
notes: A successful WRITE releases the record to the operating environment, not to a buffer: SequentialConnector.ReleaseRecord is the ONE release point every write arm reaches, and for a file any other connector may be open on (every sharing mode but NO OTHER) it flushes the record out before the statement returns, which is what makes it visible to that connector's read and, for a writer, what stops the next append landing on top of it. The keyed organizations release at the statement too: both run on the paged keyed store engine, whose WRITE (RelativeConnector.Write, IndexedConnector.Write) writes the statement's pages to the file before it returns, so the reader of another run unit finds the record at the WRITE as well; under every sharing mode but NO OTHER the statement is serialized under the store mutex (KeyedConnector.TakeFileLock sets _coherent from FileLockPosture.AdmitsAnotherRunUnit), so that reader never meets a half-written path. All three sequential write arms release (the print-control arms never did). The keyed half has its behavioural witness (kb/Work PB3414): ReadOnlyKeyedWriterStoreMutexTests asks the region host, at every page write and sync of a WRITE, REWRITE and DELETE of a SHARING WITH READ ONLY or ALL OTHER writer (the tree pages and page 2 alike), whether another handle holds the store mutex, and at every refused write of a WRITE ('30') that the mutex is back on the host when the statement answers; weakening KeyedConnector.TakeFileLock to AdmitsAnotherWriter turns every READ ONLY case red, where the source-text case StoreCoherenceTests.The_keyed_store_asks_about_any_run_unit_and_the_sequential_release_about_any_other_connector was the only one that noticed before. || kb/Work PB1587 (w1126c): cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'The successful execution of a WRITE statement releases a logical record to the operating environment' -> OK 14.9.51.4 12); cite.py --check 9.1.15 'restricts concurrent access to a physical file through file connectors other than this one, to input mode' -> OK 9.1.15 2). A record a WRITE answered '00' for was NOT in the physical file for the INPUT connector Table 19 admits beside a SHARING WITH READ ONLY writer: SequentialConnector.ReleaseRecord flushed only where another WRITER could be (ALL OTHER), so the records waited in the 4,096-byte input-output area (probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/w1126c/rsv.cob: WRITE 00, reader READ 10), and IndexedConnector's whole store persisted at CLOSE for the same posture (reader in another run unit: '10'), while RELATIVE, which writes at every statement, answered the same program the other way. Now the sequential flush asks FileLockPosture.AdmitsAnotherRunUnit (every mode but NO OTHER), the predicate the keyed store engine's coherence asks (KeyedConnector.TakeFileLock; kb/Work PB3334 moved INDEXED onto the engine and PB3335 deleted the whole store). GnuCOBOL 3.2 agrees for SEQUENTIAL and RELATIVE (probe), not for LINE SEQUENTIAL or INDEXED (stdio and Berkeley DB buffers), where ISO GR12 governs. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/IndexedConnector.WholeStore.cs#CoherentUnder (kb/Work PB3335 deleted the whole store, PB1587's arm of it included: the INDEXED organization runs on the keyed store engine, whose coherence KeyedConnector.TakeFileLock takes from FileLockPosture.AdmitsAnotherRunUnit, and whose WRITE writes the statement's pages before it returns)
